Typhon. The most fearsome of all primordial monsters, born from Gaia herself as a weapon against the Olympian gods. His body was said to contain a hundred dragon heads, and his sheer power nearly overthrew Zeus and the entire divine order before he was defeated and imprisoned beneath Mount Aetna. Typhon had a human upper body but from the waist down consisted of massive coiled serpents with venomous fangs and ever-moving heads. Fire and molten lava spurted from his many mouths and eyes, making him a walking natural disaster.

He fathered some of the most dangerous monsters in Greek mythology, including the Lernaean Hydra, the Chimera, and Cerberus. His attack on Olympus forced the gods to flee in animal form, temporarily scattering the divine council. Zeus ultimately defeated him using his master bolt—adamantine lightning—then imprisoned the monster under the volcanic mountain Aetna in Sicily. The trembling of Aetna was believed by the ancients to be Typhon shifting and stirring beneath the earth. His mother Gaia bore him specifically to challenge the gods after they had defeated her previous champion, the Titans. Some sources describe his hundred heads as regenerating or being so numerous that counting them was impossible.
